sections.title: Port of New York and New Jersey Analytics
sections.description: The PONYNJ — the US's largest container port by volume, handling trade between the US East Coast and Europe, the Mediterranean, and the Far East.

blocks.heading: Container terminal operations analytics
paragraphs: ML for the PONYNJ's large container terminals (Port Newark Container Terminal, APM Terminals, GCT New York) — berth scheduling optimization, crane productivity analytics, and yard management for the millions of containers annually transiting the PONYNJ's complex multi-terminal infrastructure.

blocks.heading: Trans-Atlantic trade flow prediction
paragraphs: ML predicting import container volumes from Europe and the Mediterranean — incorporating European manufacturing cycles, US consumer demand signals, and the carrier schedule changes that affect New York's dominant trans-Atlantic container lanes.

blocks.heading: CBP clearance analytics for PONYNJ
paragraphs: ML predicting US Customs examination selection and clearance timelines at PONYNJ's busy customs district — one of the US's most active port-of-entry customs environments.

sections.title: JFK International Air Cargo
sections.description: JFK Airport — a major international air cargo hub, particularly for high-value imports from Europe and Asia.

blocks.heading: Air freight demand and capacity analytics
paragraphs: ML for the cargo carriers and freight forwarders at JFK — predicting cargo volume by lane, carrier capacity availability, and the demand surges that eCommerce peak seasons, pharmaceutical product launches, and fashion collection arrivals create at JFK.

blocks.heading: Pharmaceutical cold chain at JFK
paragraphs: ML for the temperature-sensitive pharmaceutical cargo that flows through JFK — the New York metro area's enormous healthcare market creates significant pharmaceutical air freight volume requiring cold chain integrity monitoring.

sections.title: New York City Urban Last-Mile Delivery
sections.description: NYC's urban last-mile is the world's most challenging last-mile delivery environment.

blocks.heading: New York City route optimization
paragraphs: ML for last-mile route optimization incorporating NYC's extreme complexity — building access restrictions (delivery windows, freight elevator requirements, loading dock availability), Manhattan's grid system traffic and parking patterns, the BQE and tunnel congestion models, and the outer borough's neighborhood-specific delivery challenges.

blocks.heading: Same-day and instant delivery analytics
paragraphs: ML for the rapid delivery companies (Gopuff, Fridge No More, Buyk's successors) that have attempted to solve NYC instant delivery — demand prediction, inventory positioning, and rider routing for the dark store model in Manhattan's ultra-dense environment.

blocks.heading: Package locker and click-and-collect analytics
paragraphs: ML for the alternative delivery models increasingly used to reduce NYC's last-mile cost — predicting which customers will use lockers vs. home delivery and optimizing locker placement for the high-density apartment buildings that dominate Manhattan.

sections.title: Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Supply Chain
sections.description: For the pharmaceutical distributors and hospital supply chains serving the world's largest healthcare concentration.

blocks.heading: NYC pharmaceutical distribution analytics
paragraphs: ML for the pharmaceutical distributors serving New York's 100+ hospitals and thousands of pharmacy locations — demand forecasting, cold chain management, and DSCSA traceability for the pharmaceutical distribution network serving one of the US's most complex healthcare markets.

blocks.heading: Hospital supply chain for NYC health systems
paragraphs: ML for the supply chains of NewYork-Presbyterian, Montefiore, and NYC Health + Hospitals — surgical supply demand prediction, pharmaceutical formulary analytics, and the complex inventory management of institutions treating the most diverse patient population in the world.

sections.title: New York logistics AI technical context
sections.description: Key technical considerations for New York logistics AI deployments.

blocks.heading: NYC delivery complexity
paragraphs: New York's building access restrictions, narrow streets, limited loading zones, and extreme traffic density make route optimization more complex than any other US city. ClickMasters' NYC last-mile ML incorporates NYC-specific constraints including DOT freight rules, local building access hours, and the specific traffic patterns of each NYC neighborhood.

blocks.heading: PONYNJ multi-terminal complexity
paragraphs: The Port of New York and New Jersey operates across multiple terminals in New York and New Jersey with different ownership, operating systems, and interchange complexity — logistics AI for PONYNJ must model the multi-terminal interchange rather than treating PONYNJ as a single terminal.
